severity_definition.S1: blocks a truthful end-to-end capability product claim
severity_definition.S2: material governance or operational gap before production use

gaps.title: One stable capability identity contract is missing
gaps.summary: Semantic business capability, Scene tile capability, release entry alias and Explorer native entry use different identity semantics. They are related but not joined by an accepted canonical contract.
gaps.consequence: The platform cannot currently prove that a Scene tile, product release alias and business capability provider refer to the same approved capability asset.
gaps.next_gate: CP-01 identity ADR approved by owner

gaps.title: Scene version publication and product Scene snapshot consumption are disconnected
gaps.summary: sc.scene.action_publish creates sc.scene.version. Product delivery resolves sc.scene.snapshot. No production caller currently maps a published sc.scene.version into the sc.scene.snapshot used by DeliveryEngine.
gaps.consequence: A Scene can be published as an orchestration snapshot without becoming a consumable product Scene artifact.
gaps.next_gate: CP-03 lifecycle design after CP-00 owner review

gaps.title: Scene snapshot compatibility service is stale or unwired
gaps.summary: SceneSnapshotService writes and reads fields that are not present on the current sc.scene.snapshot model. The affected freeze/clone/mark methods also have no current production callers.
gaps.consequence: This code cannot be treated as proof of a working Scene release pipeline.
gaps.next_gate: Confirm ownership and retirement/repair scope in CP-03

gaps.title: Preview and Standard qualification evidence is not connected to release
gaps.summary: An evidence-bound maturity evaluator and eight acceptance contracts exist, but there are zero committed evidence bundles and no integration into sc.capability, sc.scene.version or sc.edition.release.snapshot.
gaps.consequence: The system cannot currently claim an evidence-backed Preview or Standard capability qualification.
gaps.next_gate: CP-04 after identity and lifecycle ownership are accepted

gaps.title: Product Release does not freeze the complete capability product dependency graph
gaps.summary: The product snapshot freezes the maintained policy and release-page projection, but Scene bindings contain only version/channel and the referenced Scene contract bytes, capability maturity evidence and full dependency closure are not embedded or hashed.
gaps.consequence: A product release cannot be independently reconstructed and qualified from its own frozen bytes.

gaps.title: Release approval is not independent and has two control paths
gaps.summary: The release policy allows self-approval, no enforcement compares requester and approver, and native release form buttons call the promotion service without the Release Operator approval policy.
gaps.consequence: Current release control is effectively single-principal on both paths, with different preconditions.
gaps.next_gate: Owner decision on approval model and native-form disposition

gaps.title: Native release ACL is weaker than the Release Operator permission boundary
gaps.summary: Release Operator requires verified platform-control authority. Direct release model ACLs require only smart_core.group_smart_core_admin, which is also the tenant-configuration admin group on a tenant database.
gaps.consequence: The source-level authorization policies disagree. Reachability of the native form in the target tenant runtime requires separate read-only verification.
gaps.next_gate: Runtime reachability evidence plus owner authority decision

gaps.title: Tenant enablement has a split write/read carrier
gaps.summary: Runtime writes use company-scoped ir.config_parameter; sc.scene.company.enablement remains a compatibility read and has a database uniqueness/record-rule contract that does not govern the active write.
gaps.consequence: There is no single database constraint or reconciliation rule across both carriers.

gaps.title: Business Scenario release can be satisfied by one released member
gaps.summary: The business catalog marks a Scenario released when at least one referenced menu is released. It does not require all declared members or a qualified subset.
gaps.consequence: Tenant enablement may treat a partially published Scenario as product-released.
gaps.next_gate: Owner defines Scenario release completeness in CP-03/CP-05

gaps.title: No governed cross-principal product delivery record exists
gaps.summary: Platform release, tenant enablement, role assignment and user verification are performed through different authorities and screens. No persisted handoff binds the exact Release to tenant acceptance and delivery verification.
gaps.consequence: A successful release does not produce a single auditable product-delivery chain.
gaps.next_gate: CP-07 workflow design without merging authorization

gaps.title: Most product asset semantics rely on Python or JSON conventions
gaps.summary: Capability native identity, dependencies, policy rows, release completeness and Scene bindings lack normalized database constraints. Only a subset of keys and relations are database-enforced.
gaps.consequence: Import, direct JSON edits or future features can create states that satisfy Python linters but are not structurally equivalent.
gaps.next_gate: CP-01/CP-02 constraint proposal and migration analysis

gaps.title: Current runtime product-release and qualification state is not revalidated
gaps.summary: CP-00 is a source audit. It did not read the current sc_dev_demo database or execute a release/qualification journey.
gaps.consequence: Historical 282/75/207 and prior snapshot observations remain historical evidence only.
gaps.next_gate: Separately authorized read-only runtime audit or CP-08 pilot
